name: Gobnat

attributes.attribute: Irish heroine, saint, or goddess and patroness of bees
one of three sisters with Crobh Dearg and Latiaran
Christian shrine in County Cork showing a sheela na gig
Celtic feast in early February devoted to Gobnat

sources: Straffon, Cheryl. The Earth Goddess: Celtic and Pagan Legacy of the Landscape. London: Blandford, 1997, 73.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gobnat, also called Gobnait, Cobnat, Abby, or Abigail, is an Irish heroine, saint, or goddess. A Christian shrine at Ballyvourney in County Cork shows a sheela na gig. This self-exposing Hag links to ancient mother goddesses. The shrine spirit is Saint Gobnat, patroness of bees. She may be a Christian form of an old local goddess. Bees acted as her watchdogs. They warned her about approaching danger. She was one of three sisters. The others were Crobh Dearg, also called Lasair, and Latiaran. Early February belongs to Gobnat. That time is spring's start in Ireland and the feast of Imbolc.

okr.objective: Present Gobnat as a possible Christianized goddess and patroness of bees.
key_results: Gobnat is a saint, heroine, or goddess of Ballyvourney.
Her bees served as watchdogs against danger.
She was one of three sisters with Crobh Dearg and Latiaran.
Early February, the time of Imbolc, belongs to her.
